candidates.source_name: 1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) / Epistle of Enoch (1 Enoch 91-108)
candidates.draft_body:
1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Epistle of Enoch (1 Enoch 91-108) (c. 100 BC)

'In those days make ready, ye righteous, to raise your prayers as a memorial, and place them as a testimony before the angels, that they may place the sin of the sinners for a memorial before the Most High' — prayer as memorial-testimony. Tewahedo intercessory practice (sustained monastic intercession for the world) preserves the memorial-prayer function as load-bearing: prayers ascend AS witnesses, not just as petitions.

candidates.source_name: 1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) / Epistle of Enoch (1 Enoch 91-108)
candidates.draft_body:
1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Epistle of Enoch (1 Enoch 91-108) (c. 100 BC)

'And in those days the fathers together with their sons shall be smitten in one place, and brethren shall fall together in death till streams flow with their blood. For a man shall not withhold his hand from slaying his sons and his sons' sons, and the sinner shall not withhold his hand from his honoured brother: from dawn till sunset they shall slay one another' — the eschatological family-breakdown. Direct anticipation of the Synoptic apocalypse (Mk 13:12 / Mt 10:21 / Lk 21:16 — 'brother shall deliver up brother to death, and the father his child'). Tewahedo eschatology preserves this family-breakdown as the canonical sign of the eschaton's approach.

1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Epistle of Enoch (1 Enoch 91-108) (c. 100 BC)

'In those days make ready, ye righteous, to raise your prayers as a memorial, and place them as a testimony before the angels, that they may place the sin of the sinners for a memorial before the Most High' — prayer as memorial-testimony. Tewahedo intercessory practice (sustained monastic intercession for the world) preserves the memorial-prayer function as load-bearing: prayers ascend AS witnesses, not just as petitions.

candidates.source_name: 1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) / Epistle of Enoch (1 Enoch 91-108)
candidates.draft_body:
1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Epistle of Enoch (1 Enoch 91-108) (c. 100 BC)

'And in those days the fathers together with their sons shall be smitten in one place, and brethren shall fall together in death till streams flow with their blood. For a man shall not withhold his hand from slaying his sons and his sons' sons, and the sinner shall not withhold his hand from his honoured brother: from dawn till sunset they shall slay one another' — the eschatological family-breakdown. Direct anticipation of the Synoptic apocalypse (Mk 13:12 / Mt 10:21 / Lk 21:16 — 'brother shall deliver up brother to death, and the father his child'). Tewahedo eschatology preserves this family-breakdown as the canonical sign of the eschaton's approach.

candidates.source_name: 1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) / Epistle of Enoch (1 Enoch 91-108)
candidates.source_attribution: 1 Enoch 99:10, trans. R.H. Charles (1912). PD. Cf. Mt 5:3-12.
candidates.draft_body:
1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Epistle of Enoch (1 Enoch 91-108) (c. 100 BC)

'Then blessed are all ye that accept the words of wisdom, and understand them, and observe the paths of the Most High, and walk in the path of His righteousness' — the Epistle's wisdom-tradition beatitude formula, anticipating the Synoptic Beatitudes (Mt 5:3-12 / Lk 6:20-23). The triple condition (accept / understand / observe + walk) maps onto the apostolic catechetical sequence (faith / understanding / practice) that becomes determinative for the Tewahedo discipleship tradition. The 'paths of the Most High' (the Geez 'arwāte ʿalê) becomes a recurring monastic-ethical category: the rule of life is walking the divine paths, distinguished from the human paths of self-will.
